newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Nov 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Nov 20.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on Nov. 20:

UNITED NATIONS - The United States, standing alone against the other 14 members of the Security Council, vetoed Secretary General Boutros Boutros-Ghali's reelection to a second, five-year term as the United Nations' top official.
WASHINGTON - Officials of the Washington area Metro system warned passengers to be more alert to potential dangers after two armed robberies on subway trains in the past week and a half.

WASHINGTON - Maryland Gov. Parris Glendening proposed cutting personal income taxes by 10 percent over three years, to be paid for by doubling the state's cigarette tax, drawing from reserve funds, and cutting spending by $280 million.

WASHINGTON - The Pentagon announced a scaled-back plan to send about 200 U.S. military personnel to Rwanda and 600 more to neighboring countries as part of a still-evolving multinational relief effort.

WASHINGTON - A former Texaco Inc. official was charged with obstructing justice by destroying some documents and withholding others in connection with a race discrimination lawsuit settled by the company last week.
